Conditions.M_text: Fresh from the booster: no scratches, no whitening, perfect corners and edges, well centred.
Conditions.NM_text: Almost flawless. On close inspection at most one or two tiny white specks on the edges or back.
Conditions.EX_text: Light wear: some whitening on the edges, fine scratches visible in the light. No creases.
Conditions.GD_text: Clear wear on edges and corners, light scratches on the front.
Conditions.LP_text: Visibly played: worn corners, scratches, possibly a small crease that does not bend the card.
Conditions.PL_text: Heavily played: creases, clear scratches or discolouration. Fine for collections that just need the card.
Conditions.PO_text: Badly damaged: tears, water damage, writing or heavy creases.
Conditions.title: Condition grades

App.metaTitle: Overpriced Cardboard Scanner – scan Pokémon cards, see prices
App.metaDescription: The Android app by Overpriced Cardboard: scan a card and see the Cardmarket price of the right printing, even without signal. Android beta, one-off licence with updates.
App.tagline: Scan a card and check current prices. Even without signal.
App.lead: The Overpriced Cardboard Scanner recognises Pokémon cards with your phone’s camera and shows the Cardmarket price of the right printing right away. Built for flea markets, Card Shows and openings.
App.priceNote: One-off licence, updates included, VAT included
App.platformApk: Currently Android only (Android 8 or newer). The Overpriced Cardboard Scanner isn’t in the Play Store yet: you get the app as an APK file.
App.platformStore: Currently Android only (Android 8 or newer), on Google Play.
App.screenshotAlt: A scan in the app: the card Altaria from Silver Tempest sits in the green frame, with its name, set, number, Cardmarket trend and the price history of the last 90 days below.
App.featuresTitle: What the Overpriced Cardboard Scanner does

recognise.title: Recognise
recognise.text: Hold the card inside the frame: when it turns green, the app is sure. It also reads the language and the card number, so it finds the right set, in English, German, French, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese and Japanese. Take uncertain cards with a double tap, and find anything else with the search.

prices.title: Prices
prices.text: Cardmarket trend, 30-day average and lowest price for each printing (normal, holo, reverse holo, 1st edition), TCGplayer as a second opinion and PSA 10, 9 and 8 for graded cards. If a more valuable printing of the same card exists, the app tells you.

history.title: Price history
history.text: Under the price you see the last 90 days; a tap opens the chart for up to a year.

offline.title: Offline
offline.text: Recognition and prices work without the internet, even in exhibition halls with no signal. Fresh prices arrive every night with an app update.

alert.title: Price alert
alert.text: Set a limit, say € 5. The phone vibrates as soon as a card above it shows up, so you can sweep through a whole box and only stop when it buzzes.

trading.title: Trading Mode
trading.text: For Card Shows: market value by condition, a verdict on the vendor’s price with an opening offer and a walk-away price, a cart per booth, bundles, trades with a balance, a day budget and your deals as CSV.

youtube.title: YouTube mode
youtube.text: A clean screen for opening videos: a big price that counts up, a hit effect above your alert price and the pack total as CSV. In recording mode the app records your opening itself; our Automatic Content Processing turns it into a finished video (see below).

webshop.title: Webshop Mode
webshop.text: For dealers: scan a card, pick language, condition, price and storage box, and it is in your own webshop, picture included. At your table you sell straight from stock. It pairs with our Webshop as a Service (see below).

services.title: Services to go with it
services.intro: Two services we run for you. Offered by {seller}.

acp.title: Automatic Content Processing
acp.text: An automatic pipeline for the recordings from YouTube mode. You upload the raw footage and get back videos ready to post.

points.voice: Commentary: a generic voice or a clone of your own

waas.title: Webshop as a Service
waas.text: Your own online shop for single cards, like this one. We host and run it; you stock it with the app’s Webshop Mode.

points.mail: a Microsoft 365 mail address with an Entra account

App.betaIntro: The Overpriced Cardboard Scanner is already used every day, but it isn’t finished. For you that means:

betaPoints.recognition: Recognition is right most of the time, not always, especially when cards touch each other or sit in binders. The app then shows you the most likely matches to pick from.
betaPoints.prices: Prices come from public data and can be missing or off for some cards. The app warns you about uncertain prices; check valuable cards before you buy.
betaPoints.english: The app is in English for now.
betaPoints.updates: Updates come all the time. Feedback to <mail>{email}</mail> helps.

licencePoints.once: {price} one-off, no subscription. During the beta this one-off licence is the only option.
licencePoints.updates: All updates are included for as long as we offer the Overpriced Cardboard Scanner.
licencePoints.device: A licence is active on one device at a time. New phone? A QR code from the app moves it, and the old device stops.
licencePoints.online: The app needs the internet once, to activate.

steps.buy: Buy a licence here in the shop.
steps.mail: Right after payment you get an e-mail with the licence key, a QR code and a download link.
steps.installApk: Open the APK file on your phone. Android asks once whether your browser may install apps: allow it.
steps.installStore: Install the Overpriced Cardboard Scanner from Google Play.
steps.activate: Start the app, scan the QR code, done.

App.storeTarget: We aim to have the Overpriced Cardboard Scanner on Google Play by the end of November 2026. Until then you install the app as an APK file; the app announces new versions itself.
